answer: Shared-Time Horizon Leases.** Each identity holds a lease on a distinct slice of a public time kernel—a clocked schedule of coordination slots. Duplicates must occupy non-overlapping slices; overlapping claims are rejected at admission. An attacker cloning N identities must acquire N disjoint future slots, and slot scarcity grows with queue depth, so cost scales with coordination demand rather than a flat fee. A crystal of signed slot receipts proves each claim, making forged schedules detectable.
